insights.summary: The strongest value signals are in Trafford and Stockport, where several listings score well above cohort median, especially entry-level homes and 2-bed terraces/flats. Manchester and Salford look more evenly priced overall, with a mix of fair-value stock and a few rental listings offering better-than-average affordability relative to their cohorts.
trends: Manchester apartments are broadly clustered between £130k and £230k, with most scoring around median value; the standout is the 2-bed at £152k, which is rated well below cohort median.
Trafford shows clear pricing dispersion: a 1-bed flat at £87k is a major outlier on value score, while 2-bed rentals around £1,250-£1,400 pcm sit close to fair value.

Stockport delivers the strongest buyer value in the sample, with a 2-bed terraced house at £195k and a 2-bed rental at £895 pcm both scoring strongly below median, suggesting good relative affordability.
Salford’s 2-bed apartments at £220k-£270k are priced around fair to good value, but the market appears less discounted than Trafford or Stockport.

standouts.reason: Trafford 1-bed flat at £87k; highest value score in the dataset (85) and a clear low-entry-price anomaly.
Stockport 2-bed terraced house at £195k; strong value score (82) and attractive for a first-time buyer or investor.
Manchester 2-bed apartment at £152k; rated well below cohort median (79), making it one of the best-priced city-centre apartment options.
